add1f3801b.why: Fold six temporary loads into memory operands of their addition and subtraction users, reading only the original addresses. Retain the last two loads to preserve the required final values of YMM8 and YMM9.

80f6297525.why: Each of the eight distinct vectors requires its own maximum-width AVX2 store, and the final RAX increment is required.

92613d1350.why: The two address results and two distinct broadcast constants each require their existing instruction.

932c153d95.why: The two multiply-and-round stages require their intermediate rounding and wrapping behavior, while the store, broadcast, and RCX update remain live.

08bbe6c195.why: All pointer results and comparison flags are required, and subtracting an unknown preserved register plus adding an offset cannot be combined in one LEA.

4b8a1264ea.why: The scalar rounding stages and final EAX value are required, and AVX2 needs separate scalar transfer, signed saturation, and word broadcast operations.

bdeafdda40.why: Each vector requires both distinct saturation operations and a store, with loads already folded into arithmetic and both scalar updates required.

33fdd827cb.why: The eight maximum-width stores, pointer increment, and counter decrement producing the required flags are all necessary.

92a3f04aed.why: Four independently preserved vector registers must be zeroed, alongside the required shift result and flag-setting RDX update.

91d357b2a6.why: Both multiply-and-round stages are needed for exact intermediate rounding, and the store, RCX update, final EAX value, and final flags are required.

490aa9f09e.why: RDI needs both subtraction and offset addition because LEA cannot subtract an unknown register, while the RDX address calculation and final comparison are required.

980b66d2d6.why: All five vector results are required, and AVX2 has no fused packed-dword addition and arithmetic-right-shift instruction.

80371e3a35.why: All three pointer results and comparison flags are required, and the RDI subtraction and constant addition cannot be fused while preserving R11.

5ab843ccbc.why: The two scalar rounding stages, both vector results, store, and RCX update are required, with the scalar-to-vector broadcast already performed directly.

2e6eeb73d5.why: The two separately addressed rows require their loads and stores, the arbitrary vector operands require both saturation operations, and both scalar updates remain live.

65f0d214c8.why: Each permutation produces a distinct required vector result from arbitrary input indices and data.
